editorial.headline: Fitness Centres: Nationally Open, but Blocked for PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers fitness facilities and independently managed fitness education—open to foreign ownership nationally, yet blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 93116 is the activity for providing places and facilities for fitness and other forms of physical conditioning as the principal business activity. Its scope also includes fitness schools or fitness education operated by the business itself. In plain terms, it is the classification for an enterprise whose core offer is access to a fitness or wellbeing facility, including an independently managed educational fitness operation within that same activity.

The activity is open at Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. That is a clear national position: foreign investment may hold the full ownership ceiling stated for this activity. The applicable national source recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder assessing the classification at national level, the essential point is not an implied restriction but the one expressly recorded here: the activity is open to PMA up to that full ceiling.

Bali is the decisive exception. A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO, and the record identifies the reason precisely: at the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope, bringing the activity within Bali’s moratorium. The provincial rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis. The moratorium cited in the record took effect in May 2026.

That produces a straightforward but consequential split. The national foreign-ownership ceiling remains 100%, yet it does not create a PMA registration path for this activity in Bali while the island-wide risk-based block applies. The issue is therefore not a reduced Bali ownership percentage or an additional local condition stated for this activity; it is a direct block on PMA registration under Bali’s permanent moratorium for the relevant risk classes. Anyone reading the national openness as a Bali registration approval would miss the central fact of this record.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness up to 100% does not create a PMA registration path in Bali while the island-wide risk-based block applies.
